primary_sources: Stanford CS229 Applied ML Assessment Guidelines

rules.rule_name: Metric Selection Alignment with Business/Domain Goal
rules.explanation: Selecting generic metrics like Accuracy often obscures model failure in domain-specific tasks (e.g., medical diagnosis where False Negatives are costly).
rules.do: Align evaluation metrics with the application domain (e.g., Recall/F1-Score for anomaly detection, MAE/RMSE for regression, PR-AUC for heavy imbalance).
rules.dont: Do not rely on Accuracy as the sole evaluation metric for non-symmetrical classification problems.

rules.explanation: A high training accuracy coupled with degraded test performance indicates severe overfitting, rendering the model unusable on unseen real-world data.
rules.do: Utilize Cross-Validation (e.g., K-Fold / Stratified K-Fold), regularization (L1/L2, Dropout), and early stopping while monitoring train vs. validation loss curves.
rules.dont: Do not evaluate models only on training data or report performance without cross-validation bounds.

rules.rule_name: Systematic Confusion Matrix and Error Analysis
rules.explanation: Quantitative score summaries do not reveal specific edge cases or systematic failure modes where the model struggles.
rules.do: Perform qualitative error analysis by examining the Confusion Matrix and inspecting misclassified samples to identify data quality or feature gaps.
rules.dont: Do not stop evaluation at top-level metrics without analyzing class-level false positives and false negatives.

rules.explanation: Hyperparameters tuned manually without structured search strategies lead to sub-optimal model performance and non-reproducible benchmarks.
rules.do: Document search strategies (GridSearchCV, RandomizedSearchCV, Optuna) along with selected optimal parameter configurations.
rules.dont: Do not leave default hyperparameters unadjusted without documenting search space exploration.
